entry.title: End of an era in Japan for classic push-button phones
entry.summary: Traditional Japanese flip phones, known as gara-kei, survived for decades with unique local features before final 3G network shutdowns ended their era. A look at how shifting mobile infrastructure impacts long-lasting hardware ecosystems and older device models. These devices have managed to remain popular in Japan for decades, offering features such as TV reception, embedded chips for payments on trains and in stores, and durable construction. However, consumer habits have changed significantly. According to a study by Docomo, smartphones accounted for 90% of mobile phone owners in Japan in 2021, a figure that will reach 98% by 2025. At the same time, shipments of such devices fell by more than 25%, falling below 400.000 units in the first half of fiscal 2025, according to research firm MM Research Institute. The definitive shift accelerated after NTT Docomo terminated the last of its legacy network services in March, following similar moves by au in 2022 and SoftBank in 2024. Docomo's termination of internet service on these devices is estimated to affect half a million people and more than 400 phone models, while also affecting other systems such as car navigation systems and vending machines. The age composition of Japanese society plays a significant role in the change, with 29% of the population aged 65 and over expected to be aged 65 or over by 2024, according to the World Economic Forum. To boost digital literacy, the Tokyo government distributed 3.000 smartphones to seniors in 2021, while NTT Docomo is running classes in its stores to teach citizens how to navigate the internet and use touchscreens. entry.title: Keep the focus ring: a keyboard check for landing pages
The IRS letter was for the company, not for me
entry.summary: A client asked to pay a company, so I formed a US LLC from abroad and waited for the letter. When it arrived I assumed the number on it was mine. It was the company's EIN. I still don't have a Social Security number. The personal number, when you have a US tax reason and can't get an SSN, is an ITIN: nine digits, starting with 9, not work authorization. The EIN never turned into one. Opening the bank account made the split obvious. For a US LLC the online business account wants: The formation documents, such as the articles of organization. The EIN letter, a CP 575 or a 147C. A passport for every owner with 25% or more. A physical business address. A registered agent, a P.O. box, or a UPS Store is not enough. That account is the company's. ITIN Club is where I found the order written out, in How to open a US bank account as a non-resident and How to get an ITIN as a foreigner. The same bank guide is also where I read that a foreign-owned single-member LLC usually files Form 5472 each year even with no income, and that the penalty for skipping it starts at $25,000. I'm not giving advice. I'm writing down the line I would have missed if the only thing I kept was the formation email.

entry.title: What the new versions bring for Python, OpenSSH and LineageOS
entry.summary: A summary of open-source software highlights from October 5 to 11, 2026. Key releases include Python 3.15 with a faster JIT and lazy imports, OpenSSH 10.6 with post-quantum support, COSMIC Desktop 1.10, and updates for Raspberry Pi OS, KDE Gear, and NVIDIA drivers. The Python programming language has reached version 3.15, bringing faster code editing and default use of UTF-8 encoding. At the same time, the COSMIC Desktop interface has reached version 1.10 with improvements to window management, while the KDE Gear application suite has been updated with fixes to popular video editing and communication programs. In the security area, OpenSSH was released in version 10.6 with protection enhancements and preparation for future encryption technologies. Also, the popular mobile operating system LineageOS introduced version 24.0, which is based on Android 17. In major news, Flathub has lifted its ban on AI-powered apps, now allowing them as long as their creators clearly state so.
